passage:
'Irfan, can I tell you something? Don't laugh.'
'Okay.'
'I'm scared of dogs. Like, properly. That's why I take the long way to tuition.'
'That's it? Fine. I won't tell.'
Two weeks later, on the same tuition steps:
'Abhinav, bhai, you're quiet today.'
'Did you tell anyone? About the dogs?'
'No. Why would I?'
'Nobody's said anything. In Class 7 I told Gaurav I liked someone, and by lunch the whole class was singing her name at me. I still don't talk to him.'
'That's rough.'
'Yeah.' Abhinav picked at his bag strap. 'So there's something else. Papa wants me to keep going to the cricket academy. I hate it. I haven't told anyone.'
'Not even your mum?'
'Not even her.'
Irfan nodded slowly. 'Okay. That stays here too.'
'Thanks,' Abhinav said, and let out a long breath.

qa.q: Why does Abhinav take the long way to tuition?
qa.a: He's scared of dogs, properly, so he takes the long way to tuition.

qa.q: Why did Abhinav ask whether Irfan had told anyone about the dogs?
qa.a: He wanted to check whether the small secret had stayed private before trusting Irfan with something bigger, because of what Gaurav did.

qa.q: What was Abhinav's turning point in deciding to share more, and was it wise?
qa.a: Finding out that nobody had heard about the dogs gave him evidence Irfan could keep a secret, so sharing the cricket academy worry step by step was sensible.

qa.q: How might Irfan feel about being trusted with the cricket academy secret?
qa.a: Irfan probably feels trusted and a bit responsible, knowing Abhinav hasn't even told his mum.

grounding: A teenage boy tells a new friend a small secret first, checks it stayed private, then shares a bigger one, still wary because of an old friend's breach.

passage: When I moved to the new school in Class 9, I didn't tell anyone anything for months. In Class 8, my best friend had read my diary aloud at a sleepover, and even now I can hear everyone laughing. Then there was Pankaj, who sat next to me in chemistry. He was funny and kind, but kind people can still talk. So I tested him. I told him I can't swim, and that I get out of every pool trip by saying I have a cold. Small, embarrassing, nothing huge. I waited. A pool trip came and went, and nobody teased me. Pankaj even said, 'Uma, want to skip together and eat chaat?' A month later I told him the real thing, that my parents were separating. He listened and didn't tell a soul. I'm glad I went slowly. I'm also glad I didn't stop at the first step.

qa.q: What small secret did Uma tell Pankaj first?
qa.a: Uma told him about not being able to swim and getting out of every pool trip by saying it was a cold.

qa.q: Why was Uma so careful about telling Pankaj anything?
qa.a: Uma still remembered the Class 8 best friend reading the diary aloud at a sleepover, and feared being laughed at again.

qa.q: What choice after the pool trip showed Uma's approach working?
qa.a: After nobody teased Uma, the small test had passed, so Uma chose to share the bigger thing about the parents separating.

qa.q: How might Pankaj feel if he learned the swimming secret had been a test?
qa.a: He might feel a little surprised, but probably understanding, since he later saw why Uma needed to be sure before sharing something so big.

grounding: A teenager looks back on testing a new friend with a small secret after an old betrayal, then sharing a bigger one once it stayed private.

passage:
Counsellor's note, girls' hostel, Class 11, Rehana:
Rehana came to see me today, calmer than in her first term. She said that when she joined, she didn't trust anyone because a friend at her old school had spread her marks around. With her roommate Zainab, she tried something small first. She told Zainab she still sleeps with a torch on, and then watched for a week to see if it got around. It didn't. Last week she told Zainab that her father has lost his job, which she had kept to herself for months. She said Zainab 'just listened and made tea'. I told Rehana her careful steps made sense and asked how she was coping at home with the news. We will meet again next Thursday.

qa.q: What small thing did Rehana first tell Zainab?
qa.a: She told Zainab she still sleeps with a torch on.

qa.q: Why did Rehana watch for a week after telling Zainab about the torch?
qa.a: She wanted to be sure the small secret stayed private before trusting Zainab with more, because an old friend had spread her marks.

qa.q: How did the counsellor respond, and why was it a good next step?
qa.a: The counsellor told Rehana her careful steps made sense and asked how she was coping with the news, keeping support going with another meeting.

qa.q: How might Zainab have felt when Rehana told her about her father's job?
qa.a: Zainab likely felt trusted and wanted to comfort Rehana, which is why she just listened and made tea.

grounding: A counsellor notes how a hostel girl, hurt before, tested her roommate with a small secret and only later shared a bigger one.

passage:
Thursday
Experiment update. Two weeks ago I told Dilnaz something small: that I can't ride a cycle, at fifteen. Not a huge secret. But if it got round, the boys in our class would never let it go.
I waited. Nothing. On Monday Rohit made cycle jokes about someone else, and Dilnaz just looked at me and said nothing. Not a wink, not a hint. Nothing!
So today in the library I told her the real one: about Papa losing his job, and why I've stopped going to the canteen. She listened, then asked if I wanted to share her tiffin, and didn't make it weird.
I know it's strange to test a friend. But last year Megha told the whole class about my braces photo within a day, and I still think about it. This time I went slowly. It worked.
Sharmila

qa.q: What small secret did Sharmila tell Dilnaz first?
qa.a: That Sharmila can't ride a cycle, at fifteen.

qa.q: Why did Sharmila want to test Dilnaz with a small secret first?
qa.a: Sharmila was still hurt by Megha spreading the braces photo last year, and wanted proof Dilnaz could keep something private before trusting more.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the library, and why did it feel safe?
qa.a: After two weeks of silence about the cycle, Sharmila shared the real worry about Papa's job; Dilnaz had already shown she could keep quiet, so the bigger step felt safe.

qa.q: How might Dilnaz feel on learning she had been tested?
qa.a: Dilnaz might be a little surprised but could understand, given how Sharmila had been hurt before, and might feel glad to have earned the trust.

grounding: A teenager shares a small secret with a new friend to see if it stays private, and only then shares a bigger one, still remembering an old breach.
